target_customer: Medical groups, billing and revenue cycle companies, hospitals and health systems that need to collect patient balances
problem: A large share of patient out-of-pocket payments in U.S. healthcare is never collected, and providers lack a patient-friendly way to bill and follow up.
business_model: B2B SaaS and payments for healthcare providers, started as digital debt collection and moved to patient financial engagement
product_category: Healthcare patient payments and revenue cycle automation

founders.name: Levon Brutyan
education: MBA and J.D. by training per his YC bio, schools not stated
founders.background_notes: YC bio lists credit risk management, health finance and B2B sales as expertise. Surname spelled Brutian in some sources.

founders.name: Max Mizotin
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page and as Maxim Mizotin in the company's 2023 press release. Search results call him CTO, not verified in an opened source.

technical_complexity.rationale: Text-message and web payment flows for patient bills, with integration to practice systems. Standard engineering with some healthcare integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and provider relationships add some stickiness but the core collections workflow was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals such as Cedar (launch Dec 2017) and Patientco (Series B July 2018) emerged or scaled after the batch; Collectly stayed independent and in March 2026 acquired Pledge Health.

market_need_then: The YC page states about half of out-of-pocket healthcare payments go uncollected. The 2023 press release cites patient payments rising to more than 35% of provider revenue from about 5% in 2000, a company claim.

identity.mascot_or_character: Billie, the AI billing agent product name per a competitor-landscape source

brand_strength.rationale: No brand press found; the name is a plain coinage that fits a debt collection origin and now an AI revenue cycle product.

pivots.to: Patient financial engagement and billing operations platform
pivots.why: TechCrunch 2023 says it refocused on billing operations as a patient financial engagement company; exact date not stated

outcome_analysis: Collectly raised a $1.9M seed after YC in 2017, then grew largely without outside money, which the CEO says made it profitable for a long time. A $29M Series A in July 2023 from Sapphire Ventures funded expansion, and in March 2026 it bought Pledge Health to add pre-service automation. It moved from debt collection toward patient-friendly billing, which fit a market where patient balances are a growing share of provider revenue.
notes: Competitor list left empty: searches found Cedar (launched Dec 2017, nine months after the batch) and Patientco (Series B July 2018) only in sources dated well after the batch, so they are not recorded. Total raised is $34.1M per the Series A release versus about $30.9M in recorded rounds, a gap of about $3.2M not found. The 2021 $3M round is reported by Banks.am and a CB Insights listing, investors unknown. 2017 seed investors beyond Y Combinator vary by source (a Pan.am snippet lists GoAhead Ventures and others) and are not recorded. Series B mislabel appears in one aggregator; the company release says Series A. TechCrunch 2023 says based in Pasadena, YC page says San Francisco.
